title: Reading Along at the Theater
transcript: A small theater added captions to its Saturday performances after visitors said they sometimes lost track of dialogue when actors turned away. At the first trial, the captions appeared on a screen above the stage. People in the front rows said looking up repeatedly made it hard to follow the actors' expressions. The theater moved the display to one side and marked the seats with the clearest view when selling tickets. It also had an operator advance each line by hand, since the actors paused longer when the audience laughed. By the third weekend, several patrons had booked those marked seats again.

questions.prompt: What bothered people in the front rows during the first trial?
options: Other viewers blocked their view of the screen.
Bright captions made the stage look darker.
Looking up at the screen made it harder to watch the actors' faces.
The text was too small to read from their seats.
questions.answer: Looking up at the screen made it harder to watch the actors' faces.
questions.explanation: 前排观众需要反复抬头看字幕，难以同时留意演员的表情。

questions.prompt: What advantage did manual control of the captions offer?
options: It allowed each viewer to set a comfortable reading speed.
It gave the operator time to add explanations of jokes.
It allowed the theater to display several lines at once.
It let the timing of the captions adjust to pauses during the performance.
questions.answer: It let the timing of the captions adjust to pauses during the performance.
questions.explanation: 观众发笑时，演员会停顿更久，工作人员可以手动跟着现场节奏切换字幕。
